facts.text: Lo Barnechea was slated to receive three Las Condes Tramway stations by 2020, a historic link to Santiago’s metro that no other nearby commune enjoys.
Nestled in Santiago’s northeastern sector, Lo Barnechea borders Los Andes to the north and Vitacura to the southwest.
Archaeological evidence shows humans have lived in Lo Barnechea for thousands of years, long before the Spanish arrived.
Before the Incas, the area was home to the Llolleo culture and the Bato tradition, later joined by the Aconcagua and Promaucaes.
The modern town of Lo Barnechea was officially founded in the 19th century, emerging from a subdivision of Las Condes.
Lo Barnechea’s neighborhoods range from affluent areas like Los Trapenses and La Dehesa to middle‑class districts such as Pueblo de Lo Barnechea and Cerro 18.
